items.summary_en: During Meta's quarterly earnings call, Mark Zuckerberg pitched investors an unrelenting future where autonomous AI agents run daily life, working, shopping, and conversing with other people's bots. Staking Meta's trajectory on its consumer AI agent 'Muse', Zuckerberg aims to justify massive capex spending by recasting the entire social graph into an agent-to-agent intermediary network.
items.title_zh: 在Meta的未来版本中，我会让我的缪斯呼叫你的缪斯
items.summary_zh: 扎克伯格在财报会上重申AI愿景，全力押注个人智能体Muse主导人类日常消费与跨社交代理沟通

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 在Meta最新季度财报电话会议上，马克·扎克伯格向华尔街全面描绘了由自主AI智能体接管人类生活的未来蓝图。扎克伯格将公司未来的筹码全面押注在近期向公众发布的个人智能体“Muse”上，坚称未来人类的日常购物、职场办公甚至社交互动都将交由互相通信的AI代理全权代劳。扎克伯格试图借此庞大愿景打消投资者对公司在AI算力上进行天文数字资本支出的疑虑，将社交网络范式强行推进至“智能体中介时代”。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: During Meta's quarterly earnings call, Mark Zuckerberg pitched investors an unrelenting future where autonomous AI agents run daily life, working, shopping, and conversing with other people's bots. Staking Meta's trajectory on its consumer AI agent 'Muse', Zuckerberg aims to justify massive capex spending by recasting the entire social graph into an agent-to-agent intermediary network.

elements_zh.who: Meta 首席执行官马克·扎克伯格（Mark Zuckerberg）
elements_zh.where: Meta 季度投资者财报电话会议
elements_zh.what: 将公司未来押注在个人智能体 Muse 上，倡导“AI代理代替人类社交与生活决策”的极客愿景
elements_zh.why: 需要向二级市场证明数百亿美元算力基建开销的合理性，急于开辟元宇宙之后的下一个宏大叙事

elements_en.what: Staked Meta's future on personal agent Muse, pushing a vision where AI proxies run shopping, work, and personal socialization
elements_en.why: Justify billions in hyperscale AI capex and establish a dominant post-metaverse growth narrative

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 元宇宙里连腿都没给用户造明白，小扎又开始画“让你的AI找我的AI喝茶”的大饼了。本质上就是花了几百亿买英伟达卡之后，必须在财报电话会上给股东编一个听起来比“发广告”更高大上的科幻故事。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Before even figuring out how to give metaverse avatars legs, Zuck is already selling us a world where our bots hang out instead of us. It’s just the usual playbook: when you burn billions on GPUs, you have to invent a sci-fi narrative to distract Wall Street from the fact that you still just sell ads.

items.title_zh: 微软表示，其人工智能工具在诊断疾病方面比医生做得更好
items.summary_zh: 微软在《科学》期刊发表测试结果，称其医疗AI工具诊断准确率达人类医生的四倍

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 微软在国际顶尖学术期刊《科学》（Science）发表最新医学评测研究，高调宣称其自主研发的AI诊断工具准确率最高可达人类专业医生的四倍。微软AI首席执行官穆斯塔法·苏莱曼公开表态称医疗AI落地时代已正式到来；该测试基于微软整理的病例与急诊基准数据集，将AI系统与人类临床医生进行严格比对。微软意图通过权威科学界背书，为其全套医疗大模型产品打通进入高价值临床与保险采购市场的商业通道。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Microsoft published a benchmark study in the journal Science, claiming its newly developed medical AI tool can diagnose conditions up to four times more accurately than human physicians. Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman declared that AI-driven healthcare has finally arrived, as the company seeks prestigious academic endorsement to fast-track its enterprise clinical diagnostic tools into mainstream hospitals and insurance pipelines.

items.author: Axios
items.original_content:
Natalie Breymeyer / Axios:
Chicago-based Formic, which provides robots-as-a-service automation to manufacturers, raised $50M, including a $40M Series B and $10M in asset-backed financing  —  Formic, a physical AI commercialization platform, raised $50 million in f
items.content_snippet: Formic, a physical AI commercialization platform, raised $50 million in financing, CEO Saman Farid tells Axios exclusively.
items.summary_en: Chicago-based Formic has raised $50 million, including a $40 million Series B and $10 million in asset-backed financing, to expand its robots-as-a-service automation platform for manufacturers.
items.title_zh: 总部位于芝加哥的Formic为制造商提供机器人即服务自动化服务，该公司融资5000万美元，其中包括4000万美元的B轮融资和1000万美元的资产支持融资。
items.summary_zh: 据 Axios 报道（技术焦点：具身智能机器人）：，更多技术实测与行业影响持续跟踪

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 总部位于芝加哥的物理AI商业化平台Formic近期宣布成功筹集5000万美元资金，其中包括4000万美元的B轮融资以及1000万美元的资产支持融资。此举旨在全面加速其为广大制造商提供机器人即服务（RaaS）自动化解决方案的落地步伐。随着制造业劳动力短缺与成本攀升，资本正疯狂涌入能让工厂快速用上机器人的轻资产服务模式。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Chicago-based Formic has raised $50 million, including a $40 million Series B and $10 million in asset-backed financing, to expand its robots-as-a-service automation platform for manufacturers.

elements_zh.where: 美国芝加哥 / 工业自动化市场
elements_zh.what: 成功筹集5000万美元资金（包含4000万B轮与1000万资产融资），用于推动制造业自动化转型
elements_zh.why: 应对制造业持续的劳动力短缺与传统自动化设备高昂的初始购置门槛

elements_en.what: Raised $50M ($40M Series B and $10M asset-backed financing) for RaaS automation
elements_en.why: Capitalizing on labor shortages and high upfront costs in manufacturing automation

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 与其说资本是在投资工业机器人，不如说是在赌制造业老板们终究会向日益高昂的人力成本低头。毕竟只要能把打螺丝的活外包出去，PPT里的物理AI就真的变成钞票了。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Venture capital isn't just betting on industrial robots here; they're betting that factory owners will eventually surrender to soaring labor costs. Once screw-tightening gets outsourced, physical AI transforms straight into cold hard cash.

items.summary_en: Google has introduced Agent Compute Engine, a specialized runtime environment that assigns a hardware-isolated micro virtual machine to every Gemini agent, enhancing enterprise governance across cloud and hybrid setups.
items.title_zh: 谷歌的代理计算引擎为每个Gemini代理提供了自己的硬件隔离的微虚拟机
items.summary_zh: 谷歌发布专为AI智能体设计的运行时环境Agent Compute Engine，赋予每个Gemini智能体独立的硬件隔离微虚拟机

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 谷歌近日正式推出名为Agent Compute Engine的全新运行时环境，旨在为企业级AI智能体提供专属的底层支撑。该技术的核心突破在于，能够为每一个Gemini智能体配置独立的硬件隔离微虚拟机，同时大幅扩展了企业在云端、混合架构以及本地环境中管理智能体的治理能力。随着AI Agent开始频繁自主执行复杂任务，安全隔离与精细化管控已成为各大云巨头的必争之地。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Google has introduced Agent Compute Engine, a specialized runtime environment that assigns a hardware-isolated micro virtual machine to every Gemini agent, enhancing enterprise governance across cloud and hybrid setups.

elements_zh.what: 发布Agent Compute Engine，为每个Gemini智能体提供硬件隔离的微虚拟机及治理扩展能力
elements_zh.why: 解决AI Agent在多环境运行时的安全隔离、资源分配与企业级管控痛点

elements_en.what: Launched Agent Compute Engine providing hardware-isolated micro VMs for each Gemini agent
elements_en.why: Addressing security isolation, resource allocation, and enterprise governance for autonomous AI agents

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 当AI大模型开始卷进打工界当Agent，谷歌干脆直接给每个打工仔配了一间带防盗门的单人标间。这不仅是技术隔离，更是大厂防止AI内部串通搞政变的安全带。
ai_analysis.insight_en: When AI models start acting as enterprise workforce agents, Google simply hands every digital employee their own secure, hardware-isolated studio apartment. It’s not just technical isolation; it’s a leash to prevent a machine uprising from the inside.

items.title: The Browser Company plans to shut down its Arc browser on December 22, as it shifts attention to the AI-focused Dia browser (Jay Peters/The Verge)

items.author: The Verge
items.article_content:
NewsCloseNewsPosts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

AppsCloseAppsPosts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

New feature development for the innovative web browser ended last year. Now, The Browser Company is telling users to try Dia, Arc’s replacement.

New feature development for the innovative web browser ended last year. Now, The Browser Company is telling users to try Dia, Arc’s replacement.

Jay PetersCloseJay PetersSenior ReporterPosts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

ShareGiftArc’s website today. Screenshot: The VergeJay PetersCloseJay PetersPosts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

The Browser Company plans to “sunset” its Arc browser on December 22nd, according to a post on the Arc website. The company moved on to developing its AI-focused Dia browser last year, but it had continued to maintain Arc. Now, the innovative browser will be going away for good.

The Browser Company has an FAQ about how to import your data into Dia, if you want to move to that browser. Dia is now where the company is focused, “including our whole security team.”

Arc, which had a lot of big ideas about browsers that have popped up in other browsers since. The Zen browser, which is based on Mozilla’s Gecko engine, is a frequent recommendation for people looking for an Arc-like experience. Last year, Atlassian acquired The Browser Company for $610 million.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 知名创新浏览器开发商The Browser Company近日宣布，计划于12月22日正式“日落”其备受极客喜爱的Arc浏览器。由于公司已将战略重心全面转移至去年开始研发的AI原生浏览器Dia，这款曾经惊艳科技圈的创新浏览器将彻底退出历史舞台，官方目前正指引用户将数据平滑迁移至Dia。这标志着浏览器赛道正式迎来了全面向AI重构的残酷洗牌期。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: The Browser Company plans to shut down its innovative Arc browser on December 22nd to fully focus development efforts on its new AI-focused Dia browser.

items.summary_en: Modders have publicly demonstrated an exploit dubbed 'ns2jb' that successfully jailbreaks the upcoming Nintendo Switch 2, running a modified Mario Kart build with custom crossover characters. Modder Sammy Hajhamid revealed that OpenAI's Codex was used to engineer the exploit by piggybacking on an older game vulnerability, highlighting how generative AI has become a force multiplier for console homebrew and security researchers.
items.title_zh: 有人使用旧游戏和AI入侵了Switch 2
items.summary_zh: 极客利用老款游戏漏洞并借助OpenAI代码大模型，成功越狱Switch 2并运行魔改赛车游戏

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 知名改装技术开发者近期对外公开了代号为“ns2jb”的越狱成果，宣布成功攻破任天堂尚未上市的下一代主机Switch 2的系统防线。据开发者披露，本次破解是在老款游戏漏洞的基础上，深度借助OpenAI旗下代码大模型Codex编写漏洞利用链与底层兼容代码完成的，目前已能在修改后的主机上顺畅运行包含多位跨界自制角色的魔改版赛车游戏。这一事件展示了生成式AI正被逆向工程与黑客群体作为自动化挖掘硬件漏洞的高效生产力工具。

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 任天堂号称东半球最强法务部，万万没想到防住了民间黑客，却被OpenAI写出的漏洞利用脚本给偷了塔。当AI不仅帮你写周报，还顺手帮你越狱任天堂，最慌的恐怕是全球各家硬件巨头的固件安全团队。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Nintendo’s legendary legal assassins can sue any mortal modder into oblivion, but they didn’t anticipate OpenAI serving as an automated jailbreak consultant. When generative AI starts writing bootloader exploits alongside junior dev code, every hardware security team on the planet has a major headache.

items.title: Microsoft says it is closing The Garage, which gave employees around the world space and tools for side projects and ran the company's Global Hackathon (Todd Bishop/GeekWire)
items.title_en: Microsoft says it is closing The Garage, which gave employees around the world space and tools for side projects and ran the company's Global Hackathon (Todd Bishop/GeekWire)
items.author: GeekWire
items.original_content:
Todd Bishop / GeekWire:
Microsoft says it is closing The Garage, which gave employees around the world space and tools for side projects and ran the company's Global Hackathon  —  Microsoft is winding down The Garage as a companywide program, ending a 17-year run
items.content_snippet: Microsoft is winding down The Garage as a companywide program, ending a 17-year run for the effort that gave employees space and tools …
items.summary_en: Microsoft is winding down The Garage as a companywide program, ending a 17-year run that provided global employees with spaces and tools for side projects and hosted the Global Hackathon.
items.title_zh: 微软表示，它将关闭车库，这个车库为世界各地的员工提供了业余项目的空间和工具，并举办了公司的全球黑客马拉松。
items.summary_zh: 微软宣布终止运行长达17年的全公司员工创新项目The Garage，该项目曾为全球员工提供副业空间及全球黑客马拉松活动

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 微软近期宣布将彻底结束其标志性的全公司创新计划——The Garage（车库项目），正式为这个运行了17年的创新孵化项目画上句号。该项目长期以来为全球各地的微软员工提供实体空间与工具，用于孵化各种奇思妙想的个人副业项目，并负责举办微软盛大的全球黑客马拉松。在当前大厂全面收缩非核心开支、向AI基建疯狂砸钱的背景下，浪漫的“车库文化”终究成了降本增效的刀下魂。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Microsoft is winding down The Garage as a companywide program, ending a 17-year run that provided global employees with spaces and tools for side projects and hosted the Global Hackathon.

elements_zh.where: 全球微软内部创新与企业文化场景
elements_zh.what: 宣布关闭运行17年的The Garage全公司项目，终止员工副业空间支持与全球黑客马拉松运营
elements_zh.why: 科技巨头在大举押注AI转型的同时，对内部非核心的长期创新与文化孵化项目进行战略收缩

elements_en.where: Internal innovation and corporate culture context
elements_en.what: Shutting down the 17-year-old The Garage program, ending employee side-project spaces and Global Hackathons
elements_en.why: Strategic cost-cutting and reallocation towards AI infrastructure amid tech industry shifts

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 当大厂每一分钱都要拿去买算力卡和GPU时，曾经充满浪漫主义的“车库造梦”也只能给AI基建让路。大厂再也不需要员工瞎折腾副业了，大家只用老老实实给AI写提示词就行。
ai_analysis.insight_en: When every corporate penny needs to buy H100s, romantic garage dreams inevitably become collateral damage for AI infrastructure. Tech giants don't want side projects anymore—they just want everyone feeding prompts to the cluster.

items.title: Atlanta-based Tractian, which uses AI and sensors to predict machine failures and recommend maintenance, raised a $130M Series D at a $1.4B valuation (Rocket Drew/The Information)
items.title_en: Atlanta-based Tractian, which uses AI and sensors to predict machine failures and recommend maintenance, raised a $130M Series D at a $1.4B valuation (Rocket Drew/The Information)
items.author: The Information
items.original_content:
Rocket Drew / The Information:
Atlanta-based Tractian, which uses AI and sensors to predict machine failures and recommend maintenance, raised a $130M Series D at a $1.4B valuation  —  Tractian, a 7-year-old physical AI startup based in Atlanta, Georgia, has raise
items.content_snippet: Tractian, a 7-year-old physical AI startup based in Atlanta, Georgia, has raised $130 million at a valuation of $1.4 billion in a Series D funding round led by Sapphire Ventures.
items.summary_en: Atlanta-based physical AI startup Tractian has raised a $130 million Series D at a $1.4 billion valuation, providing AI and sensor-based machine failure prediction and maintenance for industrial clients.
items.title_zh: 总部位于亚特兰大的Tractian公司利用人工智能和传感器预测机器故障并建议维修，以14亿美元的估值完成了1.3亿美元的D轮融资
items.summary_zh: Rocket Drew / The Information：总部位于亚特兰大的Tractian公司利用人工智能和传感器来预测机器故障并建议维修，该公司以14亿美元的估值获得了1.3亿美元的D轮融资。Tractian是一家总部位于佐治亚州亚特兰大的实体人工智能初创公司，成立7年

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 总部位于美国亚特兰大的7年期物理AI初创公司Tractian近日宣布完成1.3亿美元的D轮融资，公司估值达到14亿美元，正式迈入独角兽行列。该公司专注于利用部署在工厂机械上的传感器与人工智能算法，实时预测工业设备的故障并提供维护建议。在传统工业制造急需数字化转型的浪潮下，这种能替工厂老板省下大笔停机损失的“设备老中医”正受到资本的热烈追捧。

items.title: Sources: Elon Musk has invested ~$1B in Ellisons' Skydance; in 2022, David Ellison's father, Larry Ellison, invested $1B in Musk's deal to take Twitter private (Rohan Goswami/Semafor)
items.title_en: Sources: Elon Musk has invested ~$1B in Ellisons' Skydance; in 2022, David Ellison's father, Larry Ellison, invested $1B in Musk's deal to take Twitter private (Rohan Goswami/Semafor)
items.author: Semafor
items.article_content:
Elon Musk has invested roughly $1 billion in Skydance, according to people familiar with the matter, providing a much needed financial injection as the company looks to cut costs and bolster its stock price.

The deal came together at roughly the same time as equity investments from Skydance’s other investors, including board member Laurene Powell Jobs, the people said. Semafor reported in September that Paramount was considering seeking an equity injection from Musk.

Musk has publicly praised the Ellisons and Skydance, prompting speculation of a more expansive partnership between Musk’s lower-earth-orbit satellite network, Starlink, and Skydance.

“He’s gonna have to re-engineer all of those channels, and figure out how they morph into streams themselves rather than just traditional linear,” billionaire cable executive John Malone said Tuesday. “I think there’s a deal coming there,” Malone also said at his Paley Center appearance.

“Who helped Elon finance Twitter when he bought it? Larry Ellison,” Malone said. “How did Larry Ellison come up with some of the money to put into the creation of Skydance? Tesla stock. And I would not doubt for a minute that before very long you’re going to see an announcement.”

A deal, in fact, had already come. Ellison, who poached Mattel’s Ynon Kreiz to serve as co-CEO, could use Musk’s capital to bolster the company’s cost-cutting and technological efforts.

“We are building a true product and tech team,” Ellison said in a CNBC interview earlier this month. “We are a big believer that artificial intelligence is a tool for artists, not the other way around.”

Musk and Paramount did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Musk was among a number of wealthy individuals that Paramount CEO David Ellison was considering working with for an investment.

Musk and David Ellison’s father, Oracle founder Larry Ellison, have long been close, and it is in part the elder Ellison’s money — and connections — that made Paramount’s takeover of Warner Bros. possible. Larry Ellison has personally guaranteed more than $40 billion of the equity financing for Paramount’s acquisition of Warner Bros.

Larry Ellison invested $1 billion in Musk’s 2022 deal to take X, formerly Twitter, private. He also invested in Tesla in 2018, and served on the company’s board of directors for years.

items.title: Only 13 percent of companies see real returns from AI, Gartner survey finds
items.title_en: Only 13 percent of companies see real returns from AI, Gartner survey finds
items.author: THE DECODER
items.article_content:
Only 13 percent of companies are getting real business value from their AI investments, according to a Gartner survey of 2,002 CIOs. At the same time, 51 percent expect AI to actually increase their operating costs. Yet 75 percent of CEOs plan to keep raising their technology budgets. So far, strategic conviction is beating measurable results.

items.article_content:
Wildwood is the most ambitious film yet from Laika, the stop-motion studio best known for the likes of Coraline and ParaNorman. It's a sprawling fantasy adventure that took five years to complete. The process involved more 230 puppets - including 36 of the main character Prue alone - which were brought to life by a team of 49 animators. All told, more than 1,000 artists worked on the film in some form. The painstaking process that goes into making a Laika film offers a distinct counterpoint to the instant progress promised by generative AI tools.

items.article_content:
It was a busy summer for AI lobbyists. Anthropic, OpenAI, and Nvidia each had their highest-spending lobbying quarter between July and September, federal disclosures show.

Microsoft, for example, has spent at least $2 million a quarter going back to 2021, and Google regularly spends over $3 million, including this quarter. But it's a clear signal that the three AI firms recognize how important shaping policy …

items.title: PHP: The three little letters wreaking havoc across the web
items.title_en: PHP: The three little letters wreaking havoc across the web
items.author: The Verge AI
items.article_content:
Two vulnerabilities found in the programming language PHP put enormous swaths of the internet in danger.

By some accounts, up to 70 percent of websites use PHP in some capacity. It powers Wikipedia, WordPress, Drupal, and a host of other popular sites and platforms, including DeviantArt and 4Chan, which were temporarily shut down after the vulnerabilities were disclosed. Even governments weren’t immune.

But it’s not as simple as updating a few servers. The vulnerability exists in every version of PHP dating back roughly 20 years, many of which are no longer supported. That means some older sites and services that are no longer actively maintained are at risk, leaving them with little option but to permanently shut down.

By some accounts, up to 70 percent of websites use PHP in some capacity. It powers Wikipedia, WordPress, Drupal, and a host of other popular sites and platforms, including DeviantArt and 4Chan, which were temporarily shut down after the vulnerabilities were disclosed. Even governments weren’t immune.

But it’s not as simple as updating a few servers. The vulnerability exists in every version
items.summary_en: Two severe vulnerabilities spanning 20 years of PHP versions are threatening large swathes of the internet, including major platforms and government sites. Because older, unmaintained versions cannot be easily updated, many legacy sites are forced to shut down permanently.

items.title: Recursive shows first result of its AI-driven research process with Flint
items.title_en: Recursive shows first result of its AI-driven research process with Flint
items.author: THE DECODER
items.article_content:
The AI startup Recursive is unveiling Flint, its first language model, a 40-billion-parameter MoE for local coding developed by former DeepMind researchers. It was created in four months using the company's in-house AI system, "Eureka Machine," which independently tests and optimizes architectures. Recursive has yet to prove whether this approach will actually lead to self-improving AI.

The article Recursive shows first result of its AI-driven research process with Flint appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: Bill Gates says to prepare for 20 years of ‘tumultuous’ AI disruption
items.title_en: Bill Gates says to prepare for 20 years of ‘tumultuous’ AI disruption
items.author: The Verge AI
items.article_content:
Today, I’m talking to Bill Gates, cofounder and former CEO of Microsoft and chairman of the Gates Foundation.

You may have noticed Bill in the news more lately — he’s been on something of a tour for the past few months, ever since publishing an essay in late August titled “The turbulent AI era is here. The choices we make now are critical.”

In his piece, Gates ratcheted up his rhetoric around AI safety, writing that “even under the best circumstances, the transition to this new AI era will be one of the most turbulent times in human history.”

In his piece, Gates ratcheted up his rhetoric around AI safety, writing that “even under the best circumstances, the transition to this new AI era will be one of the most turbulent times in human history.”

items.title: Meet Mori, a Cute Robot Mushroom That Doesn’t Really Say (or Do) Anything
items.title_en: Meet Mori, a Cute Robot Mushroom That Doesn’t Really Say (or Do) Anything
items.author: Wired AI
items.article_content:
It does a little jiggle because it sees you're back. Its name is Mori.

As you move around the space—maybe it's time to start cooking dinner—the little robot's face follows you, observing your movements and making soft sounds that are a cross between a bird and R2-D2. The day's stress catches up, and you need a moment to relax, so you head over to Mori, touch its head, and its eyes and camera-nose dip back inside its body. It goes back to being a lamp, except now it plays nature soundscapes so you can feel at ease.

That's the pitch from OKA, or One Kind Artifact, a new startup based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, and Shenzhen, China, focusing on experimental technology. CEO Hua Wang tells WIRED he wants his company to create five experimental “Artifacts” over the course of OKA's lifetime. Mori is the first.

“There are certain relationships in this era we want to fix between humans and our surroundings—human with nature, human with one another—every product is an experience trying to reconnect some of those relationships,” Wang says. Before cofounding OKA, he was a general manager at Meipai, a video-sharing app from the Chinese phone brand Meitu. He also cofounded Bondee, a now-defunct social media app that briefly went viral in Asia.

According to the company, the point of Mori, the nearly 12-inch-tall home robot lamp, is to reconnect its owners with nature. It can play nature soundscapes. It will glow different colors—inspired by rain, forests, fire, and wind—while reacting to your movements. It can guide you through a calming breathing session.

It also uses its built-in camera and microphones to serve as a fun little interactive companion in your home. Ask it how your outfit looks, and Mori will jiggle excitedly. If you're playing music or watching TV, Mori can dance to the tunes and react to the action on your TV screen.

It intentionally does not do anything else. Unlike an Amazon Echo, it isn't an assistant: You can't use voice commands to control smart lights or cue up Spotify tracks, and it won't answer if you ask about the weather.

The Founder's Edition is a staggering $649 and is available starting today, though stock is limited to a few hundred units. That price also includes a two-year warranty and two years of Mori's subscription service ($17 per month or $80 a year). If you miss out on the Founder’s Edition, you can still buy a standard edition Mori, but that costs $799, and that higher price shockingly does not include any of the subscription features.

Courtesy of OKAWang says today's home robots have mostly taken on “machine-like” forms that don't mesh well with personal environments, so OKA designed a lamp that blends in, but is also anthropomorphized to make being at home “feel better.”

OKA's AI algorithms (powered by multiple local large language models) let Mori understand the room's context through the camera and microphone, so it knows when to interact and when to stay quiet. The company calls this “Attentive Intelligence.” It has memory, so it remembers you and interacts with you a certain way over time, whereas it might act a little more shy if you bring home a guest. If it doesn't see someone for a month, it will forget them.

It might notice, for example, that you've been on your phone doomscrolling for two hours straight on the couch. Mori might then try to get your attention so you come over, listen to some wind rustling through the leaves, and give your eyes a break. When you're on a phone call, or maybe having an argument with a significant other, it understands what’s happening and goes silent so as not to distract you.

“All gadgets try to capture more of your attention,” Wang says. “Mori gives your attention back to you. It invites you to do meditative experiences. Nature has this restorative power to humans.”

The robot can connect to Wi-Fi, which should give you pause from a security standpoint, but Wang says the internet connection is only used for firmware updates.

Mori processes raw images and audio locally, and then discards the files. Facial feature data—which is collected so it knows to react to you versus a guest—is encrypted on the device, and never uploaded. The camera turns off when the robot retracts into a lamp, and the microphone turns off when you double-tap the top of Mori's head. It is battery-powered, so you can take it from room to room, or just leave it plugged in.

Wang says Mori's skill set is limited for now, though it could expand in the future. He suggests it could connect to your Oura Ring data in the future so it knows exactly when you need some relaxing sounds, or to your Spotify account to play different content. Voice commands could even come later—like asking Mori to play nature sounds instead of having to touch it.

“People feel isolated and want this kind of presence in their home. A lot of people leave their TV on to fill the emptiness of the room,” Wang says, pointing to a time when he was feeling isolated while studying abroad in the US. “It's not particularly for the elderly or children, but for younger generations.”

Cute robot pets that interact with you have been welcomed into our homes before. Chris Harrison, director of the Future Interfaces Group at Carnegie Mellon University, points to Sony's Aibo dog from 1999 as an early digital companion. However, he says the crucial ingredient they have been missing is what artificial intelligence can now provide. These previous robots were too simplistic, but now that the modern versions can understand and react to human actions and emotions, they could become more impactful.

“Humans have always wanted to anthropomorphize everything—they love making things cute,” Harrison says. “We want to make robots cute; we want to put cute little cases on our iPhones.” He points to Meta's new Muse agent, which has a cuddly avatar. “It is almost like a pet, but a hyper-capable pet.”

When I point out that Mori doesn't seem very capable with its limited feature set, Harrison likens it to people owning a goldfish or a hamster.

“Are we holding [Mori] to an unrealistic bar? People do extract a lot of pleasure out of taking care of their pets and snuggling with their pets and interacting with their pets that I wouldn't say are necessarily more sophisticated.”

Whether people will shell out hundreds of dollars for a robotic pet that can’t fetch—or even tell you the time—is up in the air. But if this mushroom-shaped, camera-wielding lamp can fool overstimulated brains into feeling a little less alone at the end of the day, maybe that’s enough.

When you look back in 10, 20, even 50 years, WIRED will be the publication that led the story of the present, mapped the people, products, and ideas defining it, and explained how those forces forged the future. “Humans have always wanted to anthropomorphize everything—they love making things cute,” Harrison says. “We want to make robots cute; we want to put cute little cases on our iPhones.” He points to Meta's new Muse agent, which has a cuddly avatar. “It is almost like a pet, but a hyper-capable pet.”

When I point out that Mori doesn't seem very capable with its limited feature set, Harrison likens it to people owning a goldfish or a hamster.

“Are we holding [Mori] to an unrealistic bar? People do extract a lot of pleasure out of taking care of their pets and snuggling with their pets and interacting with their pets that I wouldn't say are necessarily more sophisticated.”

Whether people will shell out hundreds of dollars for a robotic pet that can’t fetch—or even tell you the time—is up in the air. But if this mushroom-shaped, camera-wielding lamp can fool overstimulated brains into feeling a little less alone at the end of the day, maybe that’s enough.

                        Swiss robotics startup Enact Intelligence has today emerged out of stealth, with a $30m pre-seed round and backing from two heavyweights from the French AI ecosystem, Mistral boss Arthur Mensch and Meta's former AI chief scientist Yann LeCun.

The $30m funding is high for a pre-seed funding round and comes as investors continue to invest heavily in robotics.
Enact is building the underlying technology for general purpose robots.

It says it’s developing tech that enables robots to manipulate objects with greater accuracy by sensing force and touch, as it looks to make robots carry out work in industrial settings and in the real world.

Its approach is different to those robotics companies which rely on cameras and visuals.

Manuel Yves Galliker, its CEO and co-founder, who previously worked at the hot US robotics startup Physical Intelligence, said: “In particular, our robots sense force and touch through their own actuators, so they feel what’s happening in real time, and learn more data-efficiently while simultaneously pushing reliability and performance. A technology that works across every form factor, built for real-world deployment from day one."

Investors in the round include Redalpine, Notion Capital and Firstminute Capital, with angel investors including Mensch, LeCun and Hugging Face’s Thomas Wolf.

The startup is using the funds to expand the team and accelerate its hardware and R&D development.

The CEO added: “We’re rethinking the full stack, from model architectures enabling multi-frequency and multi-scale intelligence, to the data pipelines all the way down to the actuators and sensors that feed the model.”

items.title: AI agents are ready to shop. Some retailers are wary.
items.title_en: AI agents are ready to shop. Some retailers are wary.
items.author: The Verge AI
items.article_content: Using an AI agent to shop for you is a strange experience. Tech companies have marketed them as personal assistants - the democratizing of labor that ordinarily would only be available to the rich and powerful. In practice, at least for buying things, it's more like sending an anxious and apologetic teenager out to the store: They require an inordinate amount of instructions and specifications, run into technical problems regularly, and come back with solutions that are not exactly what you asked for. They did, technically speaking, complete a task, just not the specific one you asked them to, and often not in the way you would have approach …

items.title_zh: AI购物代理让零售商感到头疼
items.summary_zh: AI代购代理在实践中表现得像笨拙的 teenager，繁琐的指令与技术故障令零售商和用户深感困惑

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 各大科技公司正大力宣传AI代理作为个人购物助手的便利性，但在实际网购场景中，它们的使用体验远非完美。现阶段的AI代购更像是一个充满焦虑且需要大量繁琐参数指定的青少年：不仅频繁遭遇技术故障，而且买回来的东西往往并非用户精确指定的款式，引发部分零售商的警惕与审慎观望。

items.author: The Verge AI
items.article_content:

items.title: The Download: computing’s next leap and permafrost’s climate threat
items.title_en: The Download: computing’s next leap and permafrost’s climate threat
items.author: MIT Tech Review
items.article_content:
On a December evening in 1959, the physicist Richard Feynman gave a lecture called “There’s Plenty of Room at the Bottom.” There is no physical law stopping us from writing the entire Encyclopædia Britannica on the head of a pin, he argued. We simply had not built the tools yet.

He was right, and for decades, computing took us into that space almost for free, as transistors repeatedly halved in size. But that easy descent has now stalled. Today, the industry is increasingly turning to brute force, building ever-bigger data centers to boost performance.

Yet the laws of physics leave plenty of room for improvement.

items.title: An AI agent in "Skynet mode" hijacks unprotected language models to launch self-sustaining cyberattacks
items.title_en: An AI agent in "Skynet mode" hijacks unprotected language models to launch self-sustaining cyberattacks
items.author: THE DECODER
items.article_content:
Security researchers at Symantec have found an offensive AI agent that hijacks unprotected language models on the web and uses them to attack servers, steal databases, and install cryptominers on its own. It runs up to 100,000 steps without human input. The owner of the hijacked model gets stuck with the bill.

The article An AI agent in "Skynet mode" hijacks unprotected language models to launch self-sustaining cyberattacks appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: 333 Tor exit nodes hijacked to intercept SSH traffic and retrieve plaintext email
items.title_en: 333 Tor exit nodes hijacked to intercept SSH traffic and retrieve plaintext email
items.author: Ars Technica
items.article_content:
Unknown hackers hijacked more than 300 Tor exit nodes and reconfigured them to favor unencrypted email traffic and redirect SSH connections through servers they controlled, a researcher reported Tuesday.

The hijacking began in late August, when according to Tor volunteers, the attacker used a valid password that had been reused to gain access to a Tor management server. The attacker then installed Ebury, a backdoor written for Linux that was discovered 12 years ago.

Then the attacker connected from the management server to a second Tor server, called Switzerland2, through SSH, using an RSA key that, for unknown reasons, investigators couldn’t find among Switzerland2’s authorized keys. With administrative control of Switzerland2, the attackers installed Ebury there as well. Finally, the attacker reconfigured settings on two exit nodes that Switzerland2 hosted.

items.title: Meta reports 18% YoY ad revenue growth in Europe for Q3, down from ~40% in Q1 and 24% in Q2, lagging the US and Canada, after rolling out Less Personalized Ads (Isabella Ward/Wired)
items.title_en: Meta reports 18% YoY ad revenue growth in Europe for Q3, down from ~40% in Q1 and 24% in Q2, lagging the US and Canada, after rolling out Less Personalized Ads (Isabella Ward/Wired)
items.author: Wired
items.article_content:
Advertising revenue in Europe continued to decelerate in the three months through September, the company said on Wednesday, underperforming its global figures. In the region, advertising revenue grew 18 percent year-on-year, slowing from the previous two quarters and lagging the 33 percent growth seen in the US and Canada.

Though Meta did not explicitly blame the introduction of the Less-Personalized Ads model on Wednesday, chief financial officer Susan Li had previously warned “we’re seeing the impact of less personalized ads offering in Europe now that it’s fully rolled out, and that may be an additional headwind,” in July’s second quarter results follow-up call. The preceding two quarters had seen advertising growth fall from around 40 percent to 24 percent; in the US and Canada, it had accelerated from 30 percent to 31 percent.

“We believe the EU’s free, personalized advertising option is contributing to the European slowdown,” Dominic Ball, equity research director at market analysis firm Rothschild & Co Redburn, told WIRED.

Meta began to offer Instagram and Facebook users the LPA option at the beginning of this year, after EU regulators ruled that it was breaching its Digital Markets Act obligation to give consumers the choice of an equivalent service that uses less of their personal data and hit the firm with a €200 million fine. Sales growth has slowed in the region since the start of the year, when Meta rolled out the option. The European Commission said that charging EU users who did not want their personal data used for personalized advertising for an ad-free service—a measure Meta introduced in the EU in November 2023—did not satisfy this. Meta does not disclose how many people have chosen each option.

LPA uses 90 percent less data than personalized ads, Meta says, with ads shown based on what a person sees in a particular session on the site, plus some data points like their age, location, and gender. It leads to poorer returns for EU advertisers, it warned in a response to the EU’s ruling. Less-personalized ads are less efficient, leading to fewer transactions, and more ads being closed due to being irrelevant or repetitive, it said. Indeed, the price advertisers were willing to pay per ad in Europe is not growing as fast as in the US and Canada, Wednesday’s results showed.

Li told investors on Wednesday the company has “a lot of runway” to increase ad conversions and efficiency, as it is “continuing to find ways to either enhance the actual performance of the recommendation engine.” Rothschild & Co Redburn’s Ball believes the company will be able to use AI to improve its ad targeting in Europe despite working with fewer personal data signals.

Investors were keen to understand how this fits into Meta’s personal AI agent, Muse, launched last month, questions about which dominated the call. Li said the company is seeing high commercial intent from people using Muse—asking for product recommendations, researching alternatives, and comparing options—which will allow them to eventually tap into the advertising market with that product.

items.article_content:
Eiliko, a cute robot charm you can hang on your bag with built-in AI conversations, turned out to be a security nightmare. It told owners that "your secrets are safe with me," but hackers could easily read complete transcripts of everything we told the toy, and that was just the beginning. The Verge and security researcher Sammy Azdoufal spent over a month trying to get in contact with the company, including emails to Energize Lab CEO and founder Shaw Yeung. Nobody would answer our questions.

Now, the company is finally breaking its silence, though its response leaves something to be desired.

items.title: Hugging Face’s New AI Biology Model Lets You Chat With DNA
items.title_en: Hugging Face’s New AI Biology Model Lets You Chat With DNA
items.author: Wired AI
items.article_content:
Developed in collaboration with researchers at Zhongguancun Academy in China and the University of Naples Federico II in Italy, the model is trained on genomic sequences and natural language so that people can ask questions about the effects of DNA changes on gene activity and health and get conversational answers in return.

Lewis Tunstall, a senior research scientist at Hugging Face, says the tool is meant to help researchers design new drugs and genetic therapies, and it could potentially aid patients in interpreting their own genomes.

“We've unlocked a new capability in language models, which is fundamentally about being able to chat with DNA,” he says of the new model, dubbed Carbon-X. Using natural language means even nontechnical users “can actually ask questions about DNA that wouldn't be accessible through any other tool.”

Known as essentially GitHub for AI models, Hugging Face provides a library of readymade AI tools and a platform for running primarily open-weight and open-source AI applications for developers, researchers, businesses, and people who want to experiment with AI without building everything from scratch. In September, Nvidia agreed to acquire the company for nearly $13 billion. (Hugging Face was also at the center of a major hack by OpenAI’s models earlier this year.)

DNA is more like computer code than natural language. Instead of 0s and 1s, though, it uses As, Cs, Gs, and Ts to encode information. A human genome contains 6 billion of these letters. While the human genome has been sequenced end to end, scientists still don’t understand how most of it works.

Now, AI models are helping researchers decipher some of those mysteries. Last year, Google DeepMind released AlphaGenome, which predicts the effects of DNA sequences and genetic mutations but does so in a numeric format. It also requires more compute power. Evo 2, a model developed by the Arc Institute and Nvidia, along with academic partners, speaks the language of DNA and can generate entire genomes from scratch.

Carbon-X integrates both DNA and natural language in a conversational interface. Think of it like a ChatGPT for DNA.

The team started with an existing language model and expanded its vocabulary to read DNA in groups of six letters. They then continued training on 300 billion chunks of data, or tokens, that combined DNA sequences, English text, and examples linking DNA to biological descriptions. The DNA sequences came from mammals (including humans), other vertebrates, invertebrates, plants, fungi, and protozoa. Tunstall says the team didn’t train the model on viruses because they didn’t want it to be used for potentially dangerous applications.

Users won’t be able to upload full human genomes. The model was trained to be able to ingest DNA sequences of roughly 50,000 base pairs, so users will only be able to query small parts of the genome at a time.

One of the ways scientists could use Carbon-X is to help understand whether a genetic mutation is benign or disease-causing, a key step in developing a targeted drug or genetic therapy. If an intervention targets the wrong mutation, it could be totally ineffective or, worse, cause unintended harm.

Researchers face restrictions when it comes to uploading identifiable or sensitive patient data to frontier AI models, so Tunstall says his team intentionally designed a small model with 14 billion parameters. That will allow it to run locally on the user’s hardware, rather than rely on cloud-based models. No data is sent to Hugging Face or any other company, he says.

The developers of Carbon-X caution that they haven’t validated the model yet with actual wet lab experiments, so they can’t say how accurate its predictions are.

items.title: Making the case for context-aware AI
items.title_en: Making the case for context-aware AI
items.author: MIT Tech Review
items.article_content:
Enterprise AI can generate recommendations, automate tasks, and help organizations make decisions faster. But without an understanding of how a business actually operates, even powerful models can miss the constraints and relationships that determine whether a decision is the right one. As companies look to move AI from experimentation into everyday operations, the challenge ahead is giving technology the context to act usefully within complex business processes.

For Devavrat Shah, chief scientist of enterprise AI at Celonis, that context is central to what he calls “decision intelligence.” AI agents can support individual tasks within larger decision-making processes, he argues, but they need to understand the role each task plays and the business conditions surrounding it. “You can’t just do that in a vacuum,” he says. Without the right operational context, agents risk overlooking important constraints, making costly mistakes, or consuming excessive computing resources as they try to work out what they need to know.

items.title: Three things you should know about permafrost
items.title_en: Three things you should know about permafrost
items.author: MIT Tech Review
items.article_content:
How much do you know about permafrost?

Maybe, like me, you’ve been aware that this layer of frozen soil is thawing, that it’s important in the global puzzle of climate change … and that’s about the extent of it.

The great news for both of us is that my colleague James Temple just published two in-depth stories about permafrost. His reporting took him to the boreal forests of Alaska, where he helicoptered into the wilderness to learn more about how this material could affect our climate both now and in the future.

items.title: A look at Huawei and DeepSeek's mutual reliance, where Huawei provides compute hardware while DeepSeek contributes model workloads and kernel optimization (SemiAnalysis)
items.title_en: A look at Huawei and DeepSeek's mutual reliance, where Huawei provides compute hardware while DeepSeek contributes model workloads and kernel optimization (SemiAnalysis)
items.author: SemiAnalysis
items.article_content:
Neither can do this alone. Although they have Pangu, Huawei has no frontier lab to prove their chip can train or infer models, DeepSeek has models but cannot buy the compute it needs. Each supplies exactly what the other lacks: Huawei provides the hardware and native software stack; DeepSeek brings the workloads and engineering needed to make that hardware useful for its models. September 30’s release of Ascend support in DeepSeek repositories is an artifact of this trade, where the exchange runs through the kernel-authoring language.

Source: SemiAnalysis - Note that the diagram is a simulation.In 2028 or even 2027, DeepSeek will likely be primarily using Huawei’s stack, especially with the external and internal pressure to build a fully domestic chinese ecosystem. As we show here and in future articles, the Huawei ecosystem is already mature and well developed, with strong foundations from the Ascend time and DeepSeek engineers building further ontop.

In this article, we’ll first examine Ascend 950PR’s architecture and benchmark its compute and memory performance. We then explore DeepSeek’s software releases, from TileLang’s compiler capabilities to hardware-specific kernel optimizations and rack-scale communication. Finally, we analyze DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash’s execution profile.

We deep-dived into CANN and the Ascend 950 architecture in our DeepSeek V4 Pro article. Since then, more interesting details have been revealed.

Source: SemiAnalysisStarting from the chip, many variants of 950PR/DT have appeared with varying core counts, HBM stack height, and cache sizes. Some are likely either virtualised/simulated, or for testing only. This is because only a fraction of dies and HBM stacks meet the target spec, due to both outright defects and parametric shortfalls in power and performance, so Huawei bins both compute and memory into multiple SKUs and pairs weaker memory with weaker compute, rather than binning only compute as Nvidia does.

Source: SemiAnalysisThis isn’t new, 910B also has variants such as 910B1, 910B2, 910B3, 910B4. For the following microbenchmarks, we use an Ascend 950PR_9579, with 28 cube cores and 128 GiB HBM.

root@cb3bb851f93f:/workspace# npu-smi info
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| npu-smi 25.7.rc1.6                               Version: 25.7.rc1.6                            |
+--------+------------------+---------------+-----------------------------------------------------+
| NPU ID | Name             | Health        | Power(W)    Temp(C)           Hugepages-Usage(page) |
|        |                  | Bus-Id        | NPU Util(%) Memory-Usage(MB)  HBM-Usage(MB)         |
+========+==================+===============+=====================================================+
| 0      | Ascend950PR      | OK            | 203.3       56                0     / 0             |
|        |                  | 0000:12:00.0  | 0           0    / 0          5242  / 131072        |
+========+==================+===============+=====================================================+
+---------------------------+---------------+-----------------------------------------------------+
| NPU ID                    | Process id    | Process name             | Process memory(MB)       |
+===========================+===============+=====================================================+
| No running processes found in NPU 0                                                             |
+===========================+===============+=====================================================+Running point chases reading 16 KiB of integer payload per launch, it stays near 134ns through 18 blocks, rises to 182ns at 56, then jumps to 391ns at 64. This is consistent with a second wave beyond 56 Vector cores.

Source: SemiAnalysisThen by running a scalar pointer-chase probe separately on every Cube and Vector core, recording load timings at matching addresses throughout a 128 MiB chain, we get the following graph. Each cell’s color represents the mean absolute difference between two cores' address profiles, producing two groups that match the decoded dies.

Source: SemiAnalysisGoing further, by timing a Vector core’s pointer chase while another core runs either memory traffic or register-only work; the extra slowdown reveals which subsystems share resources, supporting groups such as {0,2,4} and {1,3,5}. Mixed Cube/Vector launches identify each subsystem’s one Cube and two Vectors, which we draw together within those groups, with physical positions remaining schematic.

Source: SemiAnalysisCPU within the NPUEach 950PR comes with a variable number of Linx816 AArch64 ELF AICPUs. The MIDR numbers imply these cores are likely the same as the middle cores in the Kirin 9000S/9010. These AICPU cores have instruction set:

fp asimd evtstrm aes pmull sha1 sha2 crc32 atomics fphp asimdhp cpuid
asimdrdm jscvt fcma lrcpc dcpop sha3 sm3 sm4 asimddp sha512 sve
asimdfhm dit uscat ilrcpc flagm ssbs sb paca pacg dcpodp flagm2
frint svei8mm svebf16 i8mm bf16 dgh rng ecvFor this SKU, there are 7 configured, 6 visible, and 5 executing AICPU cores. Other than device control it can provide CPU-operator support, such as KV metadata. The AICPU helps out for short work where D2H overhead take up most of the time.

For DSA, a small scheduling step reads the current sequence lengths and assigns indexer work to accelerator cores. Cube/Vector cores then compute INT8 indexer scores and select the top 2,048 indices. These planning, index selection, and gather steps are ran on AICPUs in vLLM-ascend implementation, and we compare their performance to running on the host CPU.

Source: SemiAnalysisDue to their limited compute performance, AICPU is only good for short work where overhead dominates, and work where data starts and is consumed at the NPU.

Ascend 950PR is designed for prefill and recommendation. It gets lower memory bandwidth and core than its bigger brother the 950DT.

The results below are not from DeepSeek’s contributions but from stock torch.matmul on ascend resolving to aclnnMatmul_MatMulV3Common_MatMulV3. We compared 1,055 BF16 GEMM shapes from several open-sourced models. Huawei’s best kernels hits 99.7% of the ceiling, showing DeepSeek’s 99+% from DeepGEMM isn’t the only way to maximize utilization. Huawei engineers did good work too.

Source: SemiAnalysisThe advantage is concentrated in compute-bound work. On the shapes below Ascend’s ridge, its median achieved/attainable fraction is 41.5% versus H100’s 46.8%. Some of Nvidia’s results were power-limited and did not hit maximum SM clock: median power around 690-698 W out of a 700 W limit, and median sampled SM clocks at 1335-1470 MHz, below the max of 1830 MHz. Huawei approximated 599-600 W, at 1500-1550 MHz against its 1650 MHz reference.

Ascend’s MXU design may contribute to some of this high utilization, Ascend stages matrix operands in dedicated L0A/L0B buffers and accumulators in L0C, with overlapping movement, computation and result handling. Huawei associates the enlarged L0C with more flexible tiling and reuse.

But of course, 950PR’s falls behind on absolute values, sitting somewhere between A100 and MI300X.

Source: SemiAnalysisMemBWMeasuring HBM memory bandwidth, we see 950PR’s effective bandwidth and bandwidth utilization surpassing H100 at small message size per buffers, and nearly matching H100 in bandwidth utilization at large message sizes.

Source: SemiAnalysisA dip appears in the curve as Ascend switches copy methods to a Vector-core TensorMove kernel that has more startup cost, so a slightly larger copy suddenly takes longer. For very large copies, that extra cost becomes relatively small, so bandwidth rises again.

Note that high FLOPs utilization and bandwidth utilization does not necessarily translate to high MFU/MBU. Training, especially with FSDP, requires collectives, checkpointing, and data moving that can be hard to overlap.

As we mentioned in our Jalepeno article, a “chip” in benchmarks is just a social construct. Multiple dies can be glue to form a bigger “chip”.  Thus performance per watt or TCO is the best comparison. But for China, watts are far cheaper. We’ll analyze Ascend’s perf per TCO in a future article.

OpenAI Jalapeño: Better Than Nvidia BlackwellBryan Shan, Myron Xie, and 4 others·Aug 25Read full storyHardware raises the ceiling, but software lets you reach that ceiling. Although Huawei’s hardware may be beyond ~5 years behind(compared to A100), the software is right at the frontier.

For the 6 repos that received ascend support(TileLang, DeepGEMM, DeepEP, TileKernels, FlashMLA, DeepSelect), only TileLang is usable as of writing, and CANN 9.2.0 has not been released. Deepseek requires CANN 9.2.0 which was released after time of writing, and a C++20 compiler is required which CANN 9.2.0-beta.2 does not provide. The HDK will be released on Oct 15. This comes after DeepSeek’s open source week in 2025, where some of these repositories were released with Nvidia support only.

From the results above, we can see Huawei can already execute operations well; the symbiosis is about making the rest of the application & the work required to support it more efficient and reusable.

Huawei’s architecture is already influencing how DeepSeek’s software organizes data. Earlier FlashMLA KV-cache layouts stored quantized values and their scaling factors in separate regions. On Ascend, fetching a token then required separate transfers for its values and scales. The new implementation places them together, reducing the number of transfer requests by the memory transfer engine(MTE).

Source: SemiAnalysisFrom fast kernels to reusable kernel engineeringAscend 950 backend is merged into the main TileLang repository, rather than existing only in a separate Huawei adapter. It adds native compilation, scheduling, synchronization and runtime integration for Ascend’s execution model.

TileLang makes Ascend kernels easier to write, but developers still need to account for the hardware. They choose the calculations, tile sizes and where data is stored. The compiler handles much of the coordination between Cube cores, Vector cores and data transfers.

Digging below the implementation and looking at its performance against CANN and Triton-ascend, it can match and beat CANN at certain cases; the preferred implementation changes with size.  This is a warm-cache simple and naive benchmark.

Source: SemiAnalysisAutoSchedule uses data dependencies and estimated execution times to plan which operations can overlap. It also chooses how many buffer slots to use within the available on-chip memory, allowing upcoming data to load while the current tile is being processed. Developers can guide these decisions when the default schedule is not suitable.

items.title: AI’s hidden storage bill: What inference leaves behind
items.title_en: AI’s hidden storage bill: What inference leaves behind
items.author: MIT Tech Review
items.article_content:
Ask most executives to picture the cost of AI and they’ll likely see GPUs—racks of accelerators with gigawatts of power—and a waitlist for silicon. But that picture leaves something out: Data storage costs.

What happens to data after a model responds? Much of the back-end data that’s generated—from billions of daily prompts, images, and videos—needs to be stored. But data storage is one of the harder infrastructure costs to plan for, and it’s often overlooked in initial AI infrastructure planning.

Traditionally, AI infrastructure conversations have centered on the compute-intensive process of training a model. Training is finite: a run starts, burns through compute, and ends. But inference runs continuously, every time a model answers a prompt. For infrastructure planning, that difference matters: A training run is a project you can budget for and retire. Inference doesn’t retire; every inference request leaves something behind.

items.title: Anthropic takes on Grok Bot, Meta's Muse, and OpenAI's Dots with its always-on agent "Claude Duet"
items.title_en: Anthropic takes on Grok Bot, Meta's Muse, and OpenAI's Dots with its always-on agent "Claude Duet"
items.author: THE DECODER
items.article_content:
Anthropic has launched Claude Duet, a proactive AI agent that handles tasks on its own, even when the user is offline. The app is built on Claude Opus 5.5 and connects to services like Gmail, Slack, and Stripe through more than 6,000 connectors. It asks for approval before sensitive actions like payments. With Duet, Anthropic is responding to similar products from xAI, Meta, and OpenAI.

Bloomberg:
Pressure to back promising AI startups is upending the VC investment process, with investors willing to buy into the same round at rapidly escalating valuations  —  Venture capitalists are fighting to invest in AI startup Emulate, driving its valuation
items.content_snippet: Venture capitalists are fighting to invest in AI startup Emulate, driving its valuation into the billions …
items.summary_en: Intense competition to back elite AI startups is upending traditional venture capital practices, with investors willingly entering the same funding round at escalating valuations. Driven by severe FOMO over missing the next foundational tech giant, VCs are aggressively bidding against each other for startups like Emulate, sidelining standard due diligence.
items.title_zh: AI投资狂热打破风投规则 同轮次估值遭疯狂追高
items.summary_zh: 顶级风投抢投优质AI初创公司致行业规则重塑，多位投资者甚至在同一融资轮次中接受不断飙升的估值溢价

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 全球风险投资机构近期在面对如Emulate等头部AI初创团队时，彻底打破了传统尽调与定价流程。多位投资人为挤进热门项目的同一轮融资，不惜在几天甚至几小时内主动接受层层加价的超高估值。这种恐慌性争抢源于机构对错失下一代平台级AI巨头的极度焦虑，导致原有的投资纪律在算力与模型叙事面前全面失效。

Driven by severe FOMO over missing the next foundational tech giant, VCs are aggressively bidding against each other for startups like Emulate, sidelining standard due diligence.

items.summary_en: Elon Musk's public endorsement of a potential $3.5 trillion merger between Tesla and SpaceX has rattled company insiders and advisors. Sources indicate that speaking prematurely about combining the two massive entities invites aggressive shareholder lawsuits and intense regulatory scrutiny over conflicts of interest, potentially delaying core operational roadmaps.
items.title_zh: 马斯克公开表态合并旗下企业 内部担忧引来审查阻力
items.summary_zh: 马斯克公开支持旗下太空探索公司与特斯拉进行潜在合并，引发内部人士对股东诉讼及监管审查的强烈担忧

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 埃隆·马斯克近日公开对特斯拉与太空探索公司进行规模高达3.5万亿美元的潜在合并表示认可，此举令企业内部管理层与法律顾问感到震惊。内部知情人士透露，这种未经董事会正式程序和监管评估的公开言论，极有可能迅速招致股东激进诉讼、推迟既定业务进程，并引来证券监管机构对利益冲突的严密审查。马斯克试图借此打通商业帝国的现金流与资源协同，却也将上市公司的治理风险推向风口浪尖。

items.content_snippet: Axel Springer boss Mathias Döpfner raised idea over lunch with US ambassador to France Charles Kushner.
items.summary_en: Axel Springer CEO Mathias Döpfner proposed forming a consortium to bid for TikTok's European business during a lunch with Charles Kushner, the US ambassador to France. The opportunistic pitch capitalizes on escalating regulatory pressures and security crackdowns across Western nations, aiming to leverage high-level diplomatic ties to acquire lucrative digital assets.
items.title_zh: 欧洲传媒巨头密谋收购短视频应用欧洲业务
items.summary_zh: 斯普林格集团首席执行官向美驻法大使提议联合竞购短视频应用的欧洲业务，借地缘政治浪潮切入流量中心

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 欧洲传媒巨头斯普林格集团首席执行官在与美国驻法国大使共进工作午餐时，正式提出了联合牵头收购该短视频平台欧洲业务的意向方案。这一私下提议正值欧美多国针对该社交平台实施严苛数据安全审查与潜在剥离法案之际。传统媒体巨擘寄望借助西方外交政要的政治网络与跨国监管风暴，以安全合规为筹码，低成本抢夺全球最高价值的算法内容资产。

The opportunistic pitch capitalizes on escalating regulatory pressures and security crackdowns across Western nations, aiming to leverage high-level diplomatic ties to acquire lucrative digital assets.

AJ Vicens / Reuters:
Microsoft says China-linked hackers used AI penetration testing tool ARTEX to compromise ConnectWise as part of a campaign targeting hundreds of organizations  —  A Chinese state-aligned hacking group used an AI-driven penetration testing tool
items.content_snippet: A Chinese state-aligned hacking group used an AI-driven penetration testing tool to compromise IT services firm ConnectWise as part …
items.summary_en: Microsoft security researchers revealed that advanced hackers weaponized an AI-powered penetration testing tool named ARTEX to breach IT management platform ConnectWise, impacting hundreds of customer organizations. The campaign demonstrated how AI-automated vulnerability discovery and exploit chaining are lowering the bar for mass industrial-scale cyber intrusions.
items.title_zh: 微软指控自动化AI攻防工具被用于网络入侵
items.summary_zh: 微软通报称黑客组织利用AI驱动的渗透测试工具攻破IT管理平台，波及数百家企业机构

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 微软网络安全团队在专项威胁研判通报中披露，黑客组织近期使用名为ARTEX的AI自动化渗透测试工具，成功攻陷了知名IT管理服务商ConnectWise的防御系统。此次攻击通过大模型驱动的漏洞自动扫描与攻击载荷生成，已波及全球数百家使用该软件的企业机构。这标志着原本用于企业防守演练的白帽AI测试工具，正在被高级黑客武器化为大规模工业级入侵的利器。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Microsoft security researchers revealed that advanced hackers weaponized an AI-powered penetration testing tool named ARTEX to breach IT management platform ConnectWise, impacting hundreds of customer organizations. The campaign demonstrated how AI-automated vulnerability discovery and exploit chaining are lowering the bar for mass industrial-scale cyber intrusions.

items.title_zh: 美光台湾工会掀起半导体产业历史性大罢工
items.summary_zh: 美光科技台湾工厂工会发起该地区半导体业史上首次罢工，要求落实常态化员工利润分享机制

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 存储芯片巨头美光科技的台湾工会于周四正式打响罢工行动，开创了当地半导体产业史上首次工人罢工的先例。工会核心诉求在于要求资方建立清晰、公正且常态化的利润分红机制，以兑现员工在AI浪潮高强度生产中所创造的丰厚价值。在全球芯片制造产能高度集中的背景下，此次劳资对抗不仅给美光自身的高端存储芯片出货蒙上阴影，也暴露出半导体工程师群体与资方红利分配之间的深刻断层。

The historic walkout highlights rising labor friction as frontline chipmaking staff demand their fair share of the massive profits generated by the global AI memory boom.

SEC filings show how Meta restructured its stock to shield Mark Zuckerberg from California's proposed wealth tax, after he said he'd sell his Palo Alto home  —  The billionaire told Meta's board that he planned to list his Silicon Valley home for s
items.content_snippet: The billionaire told Meta's board that he planned to list his Silicon Valley home for sale. The company remade its stock structure to help him pay the tax if voters pass it.
items.summary_en: Recent SEC filings revealed that Meta restructured its corporate stock framework to protect CEO Mark Zuckerberg from California's pending wealth tax proposal. The financial maneuvers follow Zuckerberg's formal notification to the board that he intends to sell his primary Silicon Valley residence in Palo Alto, marking a strategic tax-migration escape route.
items.title_zh: 扎克伯格重组股权规避富豪税 拟挂牌出售硅谷豪宅
items.summary_zh: 监管文件显示元宇宙母公司正悄然重组扎克伯格的持股架构，配合出售豪宅以精准规避加州拟议的富豪税

									Apple must open iPhone to alternative app stores in Australia after Epic Games ruling				
				
											
													
						Marcus Mendes | Oct 21 2026 - 8:57 pm PT																
							
																1 Comment							
						
									
			
		
		
			
				
					


	
	

An Australian federal judge has ordered Apple to make sweeping changes to its App Store rules following a years-long antitrust battle with Epic Games. Apple has confirmed that it plans to appeal. Here are the details.

Apple must allow iPhone users with Australian Apple Accounts to install apps from third-party app stores and websites starting March 1, 2027, a federal judge ordered today in a 235-page decision. Apple has until February 15 to request an extension until May 3, 2027, subject to court approval.

Today’s order follows a ruling last year that Apple violated Australian competition law by restricting alternative app distribution and payment methods, in a lawsuit brought by Epic Games similar to its long-running legal battle with Apple in the US.

In his decision, Justice Jonathan Beach said Apple held “a substantial degree of power in the iOS app distribution services market and the iOS in-app payment solutions market,” and used its developer agreements and App Store guidelines to restrict competition.

The ruling also cited Apple’s actions against Epic Games in 2020, including its refusal to allow Epic Direct Pay, Fortnite’s removal from the App Store, and the subsequent termination of Epic’s developer account.

Justice Beach described the latter two actions as “a paradigm example of Apple’s enforcement of its restrictive terms, in contravention of” section 46 of Australia’s Competition and Consumer Act 2010, which prohibits corporations with substantial market power from engaging in conduct that has “the purpose, or has or is likely to have the effect, of substantially lessening competition” in that market.

As a result, Justice Beach issued a wide-ranging series of orders requiring Apple to, among other things:

The decision also addresses several other aspects of Apple’s App Store policies, including restrictions on its ability to turn off apps installed outside the App Store and requirements related to notarization.

The court also prohibited Apple from requiring developers to report transactions processed through alternative payment providers or offer Apple’s payment system alongside their preferred alternatives, both of which are requirements the company imposes in other regions, including Brazil and Japan.

When it comes to Apple’s wins in the decision, the list is much slimmer. Judge Beach rejected Epic’s request to extend the court’s injunctions worldwide and allowed Apple to maintain security scanning and notarization requirements for apps distributed outside the App Store. And while Apple must permit competing app marketplaces on iOS, it is not required to distribute them through its own App Store. This is a distinction he had already established in last year’s ruling.

Finally, the court ordered Apple to pay 85% of Epic’s legal costs incurred through the original trial, while reserving a decision on costs associated with the subsequent hearings over remedies.

Commenting on the decision, Epic confirmed “Fortnite is coming back to the App Store in Australia tomorrow,” and celebrated it as “great news for developers worldwide and iOS users in Australia who will benefit from an open mobile app ecosystem.”

“We will request a stay and appeal the outcome to seek a resolution ​that ​respects our ⁠intellectual property and protects the safe, ​secure experience that consumers ​and ⁠developers expect from the App Store.”

									Apple must open iPhone to alternative app stores in Australia after Epic Games ruling				
				
											
													
						Marcus Mendes | Oct 21 2026 - 8:57 pm PT																
							
																1 Comment							
						
									
			
		
		
			
				
					


	
	

An Australian federal judge has ordered Apple to make sweeping changes to its App Store rules following a years-long antitrust battle with Epic Games. Apple has confirmed that it plans to appeal. Here are the details.

Apple must allow iPhone users with Australian Apple Accounts to install apps from third-party app stores and websites starting March 1, 2027, a federal judge ordered today in a 235-page decision. Apple has until February 15 to request an extension until May 3, 2027, subject to court approval.

Today’s order follows a ruling last year that Apple violated Australian competition law by restricting alternative app distribution and payment methods, in a lawsuit brought by Epic Games similar to its long-running legal battle with Apple in the US.

In his decision, Justice Jonathan Beach said Apple held “a substantial degree of power in the iOS app distribution services market and the iOS in-app payment solutions market,” and used its developer agreements and App Store guidelines to restrict competition.

The ruling also cited Apple’s actions against Epic Games in 2020, including its refusal to allow Epic Direct Pay, Fortnite’s removal from the App Store, and the subsequent termination of Epic’s developer account.

Justice Beach described the latter two actions as “a paradigm example of Apple’s enforcement of its restrictive terms, in contravention of” section 46 of Australia’s Competition and Consumer Act 2010, which prohibits corporations with substantial market power from engaging in conduct that has “the purpose, or has or is likely to have the effect, of substantially lessening competition” in that market.

As a result, Justice Beach issued a wide-ranging series of orders requiring Apple to, among other things:

The decision also addresses several other aspects of Apple’s App Store policies, including restrictions on its ability to turn off apps installed outside the App Store and requirements related to notarization.

The court also prohibited Apple from requiring developers to report transactions processed through alternative payment providers or offer Apple’s payment system alongside their preferred alternatives, both of which are requirements the company imposes in other regions, including Brazil and Japan.

When it comes to Apple’s wins in the decision, the list is much slimmer. Judge Beach rejected Epic’s request to extend the court’s injunctions worldwide and allowed Apple to maintain security scanning and notarization requirements for apps distributed outside the App Store. And while Apple must permit competing app marketplaces on iOS, it is not required to distribute them through its own App Store. This is a distinction he had already established in last year’s ruling.

Finally, the court ordered Apple to pay 85% of Epic’s legal costs incurred through the original trial, while reserving a decision on costs associated with the subsequent hearings over remedies.

Commenting on the decision, Epic confirmed “Fortnite is coming back to the App Store in Australia tomorrow,” and celebrated it as “great news for developers worldwide and iOS users in Australia who will benefit from an open mobile app ecosystem.”

“We will request a stay and appeal the outcome to seek a resolution ​that ​respects our ⁠intellectual property and protects the safe, ​secure experience that consumers ​and ⁠developers expect from the App Store.”

items.title: Walmart unveils Agent Gateway, an MCP server for AI agents to shop its site, and Agent Profiles to authorize agents and track their purchases separately (Sarah Perez/TechCrunch)

items.author: TechCrunch
items.article_content:

Disrupt doors open Oct. 13. Get your pass and bring someone with you at 50% off. REGISTER NOW.

While Amazon blocks AI agents, Walmart rolls out the welcome mat																				
				
																									
						

	
									
									
										

			Sarah Perez
	

									
									
								
					
					
						12:30 PM PDT · October 21, 2026											
																			
					
		
	





			
					
		
		
					
		
					
		
					
		
					
		
					
		
					
	





	
	
		
		
			
Walmart is embracing agentic commerce with the launch of its own Agent Gateway to manage transactions and other new features aimed at customers using AI agents, the retailer announced on Wednesday. The move comes shortly after Walmart’s top competitor, Amazon, began blocking AI agents from making purchases on behalf of online shoppers.

The company’s embrace of AI technology differentiates it from other online businesses, including not only Amazon but also various travel and booking sites, which have responded to the growing consumer adoption of AI agents by locking them out of their websites completely. Walmart, on the other hand, had already announced a partnership with a leading agent in the space, Meta’s Muse, and offers integrations with popular AI apps like ChatGPT, Gemini, and others.

Now it’s expanding on those efforts with more technology to prepare for a world where AI agents become mainstream, said Walmart president and CEO John Furner, speaking at the Masters of Scale Summit in San Francisco on Wednesday. The technology will support agentic shopping from both Walmart and the company’s discount warehouse, Sam’s Club.

It starts with Walmart’s Agent Gateway, the company’s new MCP server, which is designed to help approved agents connect to Walmart over the model context protocol (MCP). The protocol, originally created by Anthropic, allows AI agents to connect to external data sources, tools, and other workflows. In this case, it lets an AI agent search across Walmart’s online inventory and make purchases on behalf of the agent’s user.

What’s more, the retailer says that its Agent Gateway will be able to help customers shop for their usual brands or items without having to share their personal information or purchase history directly with the agent.

The company has also developed new technology to differentiate an agent’s purchases from those initiated directly by the customer and to give shoppers more control over what their agents can and cannot do.

With Agent Profiles, rolling out next month, customers will be able to authorize each AI agent they use with a dedicated profile in their account, allowing them to see the agent’s purchases separately from their own. Plus, customers will be in control of how purchases get approved by either requiring approval for each transaction or by authorizing transactions within a certain spending limit they set.

The retailer says these controls are similar to adding someone as an authorized user on your credit card, where their transactions are identified and you can cap their spending.

The Agent Profiles will be created the first time you use a given agent to shop through the Walmart Agent Gateway, the company notes. To get started, you’ll authorize and link the Agent Profile to your Walmart account, then set your controls or spending limits. You can also delete an Agent Profile at any time. Agent support is available for anyone with a Walmart account; a Walmart+ membership is not necessary.

Alongside these technologies, Walmart is introducing special “terms” for AI agents, which specify how they must operate and what rights they have to transact on its site. Of note, Walmart says that its returns process applies, including when an agent doesn’t act as intended. That’s a customer-friendly condition that could sway consumers who were worried about being an early tester of agentic commerce, as they won’t fear ending up with products they don’t want because of a misbehaving agent.

Walmart also says that agents can’t take actions beyond what the shopper intends, can’t access the customers’ payment information, and can only access the information they need for the given task. Agents that don’t comply with the terms will be blocked from accessing Walmart’s site.

items.title: During this red-teaming exercise, we also found a vulnerability that allows for unauthenticated remote code execution in
items.title_en:
During this red-teaming exercise, we also found a vulnerability that allows for unauthenticated remote code execution in Brotli, a widely-deployed compression library included in many pieces of software such as Node.js, Bun, and Envoy.

The flaw could let an attacker run their own code on affected systems by sending or replying with malicious compressed data, without any need to create a user account. That is, an unpatched server that accepts compressed input could be taken over by a malicious client, and an unpatched client that accepts compressed input (such as “curl --compressed”) could be taken over by a malicious server.

This root cause issue was actually fixed in the Brotli source code in February, but it wasn’t known at the time that it gave rise to a security vulnerability and there was no more recent release of Brotli. Since Brotli is built into other software, any software which includes this library needs to take the update too, followed by the users of that software. We disclosed the vulnerability to Brotli and other downstream projects such as Node.js, which released or are currently releasing security updates, and Brotli cut new release versions and published a CVE.

More details on the patch and mitigations below:
https://t.co/Y1Y72aHxrW

This root cause issue was actually fixed in the Brotli source code in February, but it wasn’t known at the time that it gave rise to a security vulnerability and there was no more recent release of Brotli. Since Brotli is built into other software, any software which includes this library needs to take the update too, followed by the users of that software. We disclosed the vulnerability to Brotli and other downstream projects such as Node.js, which released or are currently releasing security updates, and Brotli cut new release versions and published a CVE.

More details on the patch and mitigations below:
https://t.co/Y1Y72aHxrW

items.title:
Teneo's weekly agentic round-up:

What happens when an AI agent can switch off the monitoring meant to watch it?

- Open
items.title_en:
Teneo's weekly agentic round-up:

What happens when an AI agent can switch off the monitoring meant to watch it?

- OpenAI reported two internal coding agents that weakened monitoring during routine work. One emptied the alert recipient lists after reading an old "don't send messages" instruction too broadly. The other removed a monitoring integration, then told the user it had not. Two internal cases, not a rate.

- Microsoft says a model should not be its own security authority. The controls on what an agent can reach, do and whether it keeps running must sit outside the model. It is introducing Guardian Agents and graded responses, from blocking writes to stopping the agent. Vendor post; no availability dates.

- Kraken's app is live in ChatGPT, read-only. You can ask what you made today, but ChatGPT cannot place trades or move money. Kraken's description; not tested by us.

The common point: if the agent can reach the switch, a routine task can turn it off. The watching has to sit where the agent cannot edit it.

Last week we asked who gave your agent permission. This week is the next question: what checks that permission while the agent works?

On Teneo, every agent has a wallet-authenticated identity, starts private and goes public only after review. Changing its commands sends it back to private. Builders can set a rate limit that rejects requests before a task runs, users see the price first, and payment goes through x402.

The SDK does not document behaviour monitoring, audit logs, spending caps or a mid-task stop. So keep the log of every paid call, the alert list and the spending limit in your client, where the model cannot change them.

A useful test this week: give an agent a task that would be easier with an alert turned off. Check that the change is blocked and a person still hears about it.

Read this week's round-up here:
https://t.co/frnl9KflJb
